claims.text: The stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr is governed by the degree of chemical short-range order.
Annealing HfNbTaTiZr at approximately 600 °C for 30–120 minutes promotes chemical short-range order or local solute clustering.
Chemical short-range order changes local interatomic environments and dislocation core structures.
Changes in local chemical environments and electronic bonding can modify the alloy's elastic stiffness.
CSRO increases the barrier to dislocation motion and therefore raises yield strength.
CSRO reduces the high-temperature creep rate of HfNbTaTiZr.
CSRO-induced dislocation pinning increases the microhardness measured after cold rolling.
Annealed, CSRO-containing samples will have higher yield strength than rapidly quenched, disordered samples.
Annealed, CSRO-containing samples will have lower creep rates than rapidly quenched, disordered samples.
Annealed samples will show discernible elastic-modulus shifts relative to the quenched baseline.
Annealed samples will show discernible thermal-expansion shifts relative to the quenched baseline.
CSRO can produce anisotropic thermal-expansion behavior through changes in bonding stiffness and local lattice parameters.
A fully homogenized and rapidly quenched HfNbTaTiZr sample has minimal CSRO and is an effectively disordered baseline.
Rapid quenching freezes the chemically disordered state of HfNbTaTiZr.
Changes in mechanical and thermoelastic responses should correlate with CSRO degree as annealing time is varied.
Secondary microstructural heterogeneities may influence the measured behavior.
